chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Aban, from Al-Hasan al-Attar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man slandered a group of people all together, so he said with one word. I said: Yes. He said: He receives one hadd (flogging). And if he distinguished between them in the slander, a hadd is inflicted on each one of them.

key_terms.حَدًّا: A fixed punishment, specifically flogging (usually 80 lashes) for slander
key_terms.فَرَّقَ: To distinguish or separate (in the context of addressing individuals separately)
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To slander or accuse of zina (unlawful sexual intercourse)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for slandering a group collectively versus individually in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies the application of the hadd al-rami (flogging for slander) by distinguishing between collective and individual accusations. It establishes that a single utterance targeting a group incurs only one penalty, whereas specifying individuals individually triggers separate penalties for each, reflecting the principle of proportional justice in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling ensures that the punishment aligns with the specific intent and scope of the accuser's statement.
